A1.justification: Both PDFs describe successive versions of the same neural-ODE and negative-feedback work, renamed from COTODE to DeNOTS. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: Section 4, Tables 1–2 and Appendix C report original classification experiments on six datasets and negative-feedback, interpolation and kernel-scale analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.5 and B report original classification, regression, depth, robustness and Monte Carlo results. The separately attributed NCDE Sepsis scores do not negate these original results.

M1.justification: The negated-GRU feedback mechanism is retained. However, v2 replaces squared-exponential GP interpolation with cubic splines and introduces explicit depth-dependent timestamp rescaling in Algorithm 1. These alter central parts of the forward procedure beyond renaming the model.

E1.justification: v2 retains WISDM under the name HAR, removes Age, Churn, HSBC, Gender and Retail, and adds PhysioNet Sepsis classification and synthetic Pendulum regression. It also introduces localized missing-observation and noisy-observation test scenarios.

E2.justification: GRU/RNN remains, but RNN Decay and RNN ODE disappear from the benchmark comparisons. v2 adds a Transformer with rotary embeddings, Mamba implemented as Mamba2, and NCDE, including on retained WISDM/HAR coverage. Figure 1 also evaluates the constant-feedback alternative that v1 only discusses.

E3.justification: WISDM changes from 15-second, 20 Hz windows containing 300 observations to three-minute, 4 Hz sequences containing 720 observations; HAR evaluation retains accuracy but drops AUROC. v2 adds depth configurations, reduced-sample and shortened-sequence controls, and localized attacks with comparisons matched on clean-data performance. Reported backpropagation changes from adjoint-based to AutoDiff.

E4.justification: v1's interpolation-regime and kernel-scale ablations and PCA trajectory examples disappear. v2 expands feedback analysis through depth and constant-feedback comparisons, adds HAR noise/drop attacks, Pendulum overfitting and sequence-length diagnostics, and empirical checks of the irregular-grid assumption in Appendix A.5.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means and standard deviations over three runs, with v2 retaining the deviations in Appendix Table 4. v2 explicitly identifies different seeds and adds ten-seed attack averaging with shaded variability in Figure 4 and Appendix B.5.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are largely replaced. v1 Table 2 reports COTODE GP WISDM accuracy of 0.36 ± 0.02; v2 Table 4 reports DeNOTS-1 HAR accuracy of 0.48 ± 0.05 under changed preprocessing and method, preventing a same-setting performance comparison. v2 adds Pendulum R2 of 0.64 and Sepsis AUROC of 0.93 for DeNOTS-20, plus depth, attack and diagnostic results, while financial and Retail results disappear.

T1.justification: Much of v1's GP interpolation and minimax analysis survives in Appendix A.4. However, v2 replaces the central linear-dynamics error analysis with Lipschitz-based stability, forgetfulness and robustness theorems and proofs, notably Theorems 3.4, 3.5 and 3.9. v1's Lemma 3.1 becomes Assumption 3.6, supplemented by the restricted-setting Lemma A.9.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes novel GP-based continuous event trajectories and superiority on sufficiently long sequences. v2 centers its contributions on stable integration at greater depth, nonaccumulating discretization uncertainty, and forgetting irrelevant history while retaining useful information. These substantially redefine the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 explains weaker Gender/Retail performance through short sequences and discusses kernel-scale instability. v2 adds interpretations involving depth-induced overfitting, attack-location-dependent forgetting, and memory or convergence problems on Pendulum. It also explicitly acknowledges slow execution in Section 7 and Appendix B.2.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's brief library and repository description, v2 Appendix B specifies hidden size 32, one-layer configurations, Dopri5 tolerance, Adam learning rate, validation-based stopping, normalization, missing-value handling and static-feature initialization. It updates the repository reference and describes automated scripts and YAML configurations. These are largely additional disclosures, not evidence that every newly specified setting changed.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from transactional event sequences and temporal point processes toward deep neural ODEs, state-space models and robustness. v2 adds substantive discussion and citations concerning Mamba, integration-depth restrictions and adversarial evaluation, while removing much of v1's financial and neural point-process literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around depth and stability. Method and theory become separate sections, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, and the appendices are reorganized. Dedicated limitations and impact sections are added.

P2.justification: v1's continuity cartoon, PCA trajectories and kernel-scale plot disappear. v2 adds depth-performance and eight-panel attack figures, revises the trajectory-norm comparisons, and updates and relocates the pipeline diagram. Tables are substantially reorganized, including main-text means and appendix uncertainty reporting, while appendices change to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited validation with modern comparators, depth and robustness controls, and detailed reproducibility information. However, its stronger central guarantees have unresolved support problems: Appendix A identifies the feedback matrix with a state-dependent gate but treats it as fixed in subsequent proofs, and Theorem 3.9 states positive feedback where its proof assumes negative feedback. These weaknesses affect the revised contribution's theoretical foundation, making the net quality effect uncertain despite clear empirical and documentation gains.
